papers.title: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design
papers.abstract: In high-dimensional, PDE-constrained design, interpolating between known feasible solutions can reveal trade-offs without repeating expensive optimization campaigns. In stellarator design for fusion energy, direct interpolation of plasma boundary parameters can violate physical constraints even when both endpoints are feasible. Learned latent representations can capture nonlinear relationships among design variables, but latent interpolation can still cross infeasible regions, and conditioning on target metrics can become inconsistent with the decoded design. We introduce CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training, paired with self-consistent inference that aligns conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. Geometric benchmarks show the benefit of regularizing latent interpolants. In stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, CHORD reaches up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility, compared with 50% for an unregularized conditional VAE and 28% for direct interpolation of boundary parameters. Ablations show that both ingredients are needed for this gain. Beyond interpolation, latent-space optimization finds simulator-feasible designs, while self-consistent sampling produces more diverse feasible alternatives. On the ConStellaration benchmark, chord-regularized models with linear conditioning reuse data from five optimization campaigns and simulator-labeled rescalings to populate the Pareto front more densely. After low-fidelity screening, 93% of 1.2k generated candidates pass the benchmark's high-fidelity feasibility test. We release code and over 600k designs for stellarator generation, surrogate training, and front-filling evaluation. These results support feasibility-aware latent learning for exploring constrained design trade-offs.

papers.title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
papers.abstract: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

papers.title: High-energy electron-positron beam collisions with large-angle disruptions
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the beam and field dynamics in high-energy electron-positron collisions are governed by a new dimensionless parameter $\varepsilon$. In the high-disruption regime, particles are deflected transversely at angles of order $\varepsilon$ while simultaneously undergoing longitudinal deceleration which scales as $\varepsilon^2$, accompanied by the emergence of a longitudinal electric field with amplitude proportional to $\varepsilon$. We identify the large-angle disruptions ($\varepsilon \ge 1$) as a novel extreme regime in which transverse motion becomes strongly relativistic and the braking effect fully arrests, and subsequently reverses, beam propagation. Our theoretical model is in good agreement with three-dimensional electromagnetic particle-in-cell simulations. Existing beam-beam studies are valid only in the $\varepsilon \ll 1$ limit. For proposed plasma-based linear colliders operating in the quantum regime, notable beam-beam effects generate low-energy secondary particles whose $\varepsilon$ can approach unity; the collision dynamics and behavior of these particles may therefore require fully electromagnetic particle-in-cell simulations for accurate modeling.

papers.title: Measuring the tug-of-war between two nonlinearities in a monopolar plasma vortex
papers.abstract: From planetary atmospheres to magnetized plasmas, single-core vortices organize flows and transport heat and matter. Understanding their persistence requires identifying the nonlinear interactions that sustain a single core. The Charney--Hasegawa--Mima equation, shared by drift waves and Rossby waves, admits steadily propagating localized vortex solutions only in dipole form. Theories of monopolar drift vortices attribute the additional nonlinearity to either the electron-temperature gradient or density-profile curvature, but their respective roles remain experimentally unresolved. Here we show that the coupling sustaining a monopolar drift vortex results from the near cancellation of two much larger nonlinear contributions. We measure three-wave coupling among the vortex harmonics using simultaneous probe signals acquired around the full azimuth of a laboratory plasma and compare it with predictions of an extended drift-wave equation derived for the measured equilibrium conditions. The equation reproduces the sign, magnitude and triad dependence of the observed coupling without adjustable parameters, whereas neither contribution alone accounts for the measured coupling pattern. This coupling transfers fluctuation power from the linearly driven fundamental to damped harmonics, maintaining the single-core waveform. These results establish an experimental route to distinguishing mechanisms that produce similar vortex structures by resolving the nonlinear interactions within them.

papers.title: Exact force-free three-dimensional toroidal equilibria and the sawtooth q(0) problem
papers.abstract: We construct exact, closed-form solutions of curl of B=lambda B with nested toroidal flux surfaces around a closed magnetic axis, finite rotational transform and, in general, no continuous Euclidean symmetry. They are counterexamples to Grad's conjecture in its pressureless form. Inside a regular flux surface that fits in a ball of radius r_b with |lambda| r_b<4.49, each is the unique minimum of magnetic energy at fixed toroidal flux and helicity, so each is a Taylor state. The rotational transform is a ratio of one-dimensional integrals. Our primary application is the sawtooth q(0) problem in tokamaks. In one configuration, q crosses unity on a smooth torus of closed field lines, with no island and no current sheet. Across the family, minimum-energy fixed-boundary states with q(0)<1<q_wall exist; in our scans q(0) reaches 0.84 at tight aspect ratio and about 0.94 at conventional aspect ratio. At comparable helicity-to-flux ratio, configurations with different boundary shapes have either sign of the magnetic shear. These fixed-boundary equilibria are candidates for relaxed cores, which need not be axisymmetric. Their dynamical accessibility and their matching to the surrounding plasma remain open.

papers.title: Toward divertor plasma detachment in pure D-T plasma in fusion reactor with H-mode-like plasma confinement
papers.abstract: The conditions between the separatrix plasma density and the heat flux into the scrape-off layer region allowing reaching an ultimate divertor plasma detachment with H-mode confinement in pure hydrogen (deuterium or the mixture of deuterium and tritium) plasma are obtained. Estimates for a number of present-day tokamaks show that this regime is accessible at separatrix plasma densities below or around the empirical density limit. Moreover, they are in reasonable agreement with the data from the AUG tokamak, where detachment was reached in pure deuterium plasma. However, in future reactors, such as ITER, ARC, and EU-DEMO, it would require densities exceeding this empirical density limit. Therefore, additional measures are needed for future reactors, such as operation above the density limit, which, according to recent experimental data, may not be a hard operational boundary, turbulence induced broadening of the heat flux width and reduction of the parallel heat flux in the long legs of advanced divertor configurations. Their successful implementation would open the possibility for a more efficient reactor design.

papers.title: Streaming instabilities and electron transport in electron transpiration cooling
papers.abstract: Electron transpiration cooling requires emitted electrons to travel through a surrounding plasma, where their relative motion with background electrons can drive streaming instabilities. We investigate these instabilities using particle-in-cell simulations with Monte Carlo collisions in a finite helium plasma. Lower neutral densities show pronounced wave activity, while higher densities give smoother electron distributions. A multifluid model constructed from simulated velocity distributions captures the frequency scale and decay direction in selected cases, but underestimates the separate driving and absorbing responses of electron populations. Distinguishing fast and slow emitted electrons and normalizing the field amplitude by the expanding two-peak length improves the low-wavenumber growth comparison, while discrepancies remain. Spatial growth estimates show that finite propagation distance also limits amplification. Strong late-time current fluctuations can coexist with nearly complete mean anode collection. These findings connect streaming instability to electron transport in the cooling model and show both the usefulness and limitations of a fluid description.

papers.title: The effects of closure parameter on the properties of kinetic range plasma turbulence
papers.abstract: Simulations of plasmas such as the solar wind require an accurate representation of kinetic physics given the lack of frequent collisions. Fully kinetic treatments are computationally expensive and necessarily confine simulations to small domain sizes. A good compromise is to utilise higher-order fluid-moment models such as the 10-moment model. This model retains all physics up to the second moment, with the moment hierarchy closed by approximating the heat flux. One choice is to use a model for the divergence of the heat flux, $\partial_m q_{ijm} \approx v_t |k_0|(\mathbf{P}_{ij}-p\delta_{ij})$, with a free parameter $k_0$, called the ``closure parameter''. We study the effects of this closure parameter on the properties of turbulence, combined with artificial ion-electron mass ratios. We show that the heating of the two plasma species is affected by the choice of the closure parameter. For all combinations of closure parameters, the relative compressive and incompressive heating rates are affected even for realistic mass ratios. The effects are more prominent for lower mass ratios and diminish when approaching realistic mass ratios.

papers.title: Global full-f gyrokinetic analysis of energetic-particle-driven Alfv\'en eigenmodes and their phase-space drive with GYSELA
papers.abstract: We investigate the linear stability of energetic-particle (EP) driven Alfv\'en eigenmodes and the wave-particle interaction in phase space, using the newly implemented energetic-particle module in the electromagnetic global full-f gyrokinetic code GYSELA. The coupled gyrokinetic-Maxwell system self-consistently evolves the EP species alongside thermal ions and kinetic electrons, retaining finite-orbit-width and global profile effects. To mitigate the relaxation of the initial distribution in global full-f models, a canonical Maxwellian initialisation is employed, which strongly reduces this relaxation and the associated change of the drive. The framework is verified against the ITPA-TAE and the reversed-shear NLED-AUG cases, including scans in EP temperature and density. The agreement with published multi-code results is quantitative for the ITPA-TAE case and qualitative for the NLED-AUG case, where a reversed-shear Alfv\'en eigenmode (RSAE) is found near $q_{\rm min}$. Beyond verification, we use a constants-of-motion (CoM) diagnostic to project the gyrocentre distribution and the local wave-particle power exchange ($P = -\mathbf{J}\cdot\mathbf{E}$) onto invariant space. This identifies the orbit classes and resonances that interact with the mode. For the ITPA-TAE, deeply co-passing orbits dominate the drive. For the NLED-AUG RSAE, counter-passing orbits drive the mode and co-passing orbits damp it, and the sign of the exchange follows that of the linear EP drive. These results provide a basis for future global full-f studies of nonlinear energetic-particle transport and mode saturation.

papers.title: Annular-curvature effects on high-frequency azimuthal fluctuations in 3D PIC simulations of Hall-thruster plasmas
papers.abstract: Azimuthal instabilities and associated plasma fluctuations play an important role in anomalous cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters. Kinetic studies often approximate the annular discharge using local Cartesian domains, but the influence of the neglected curvature on threedimensional fluctuation dynamics remains insufficiently quantified. Here, three-dimensional cylindrical electrostatic particle-in-cell simulations assess this geometric effect in a reduced channel-plume model by varying the minimum computational-domain radius rmin at fixed channel width and imposed magnetic-field profile. The dominant channel wavenumbers on the centerline-reference scale remain similar, while pronounced radial amplitude asymmetry develops in the smaller-radius configurations. At rmin = 10 cm and 2 cm, the outer-channel electric-field amplitudes in the dominant wavenumber band exceed the inner-channel values by 26% and 53%, respectively. In the plume, low-wavenumber fluctuations favor the inner region, whereas high-wavenumber components favor the outer region. Density-electric-field covariance is preferentially concentrated in the outer channel and inner plume, with outer-to-inner magnitude ratios of 2.71 and 0.58 at rmin = 2 cm. These persistent spatial preferences connect the geometric redistribution of fluctuations to the correlated axial ExB drift contribution. For the 1.28 cm channel width studied, these results support retaining cylindrical geometry at rmin = 10 cm and 2 cm to resolve local fluctuations and transport-related correlations, even when the imposed magnetic-field profile is unchanged.

papers.title: Whistler instability driven by electron trapping in magnetic dips
papers.abstract: Using fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations, we show how free energy released by an ion-scale instability reaches electron scales through its effect on the electron distribution. An initial ion temperature anisotropy drives partly compressional ion cyclotron waves, which form magnetic dips. Electrons trapped in these dips develop an enhanced temperature anisotropy and butterfly-shaped distributions, similar to those observed by spacecraft in the Earth's magnetosheath. By tracking the energy transfer in velocity space, we show that the gradients created by trapping drive whistler waves through cyclotron resonance. The whistlers in turn scatter the electrons in pitch angle, flattening velocity-space gradients and heating the electrons along the magnetic field. As a result, the electron anisotropy drops to about half of the double-adiabatic prediction once the whistler power peaks. Our results show that it is the shape of the electron distribution in magnetic dips, rather than its temperature anisotropy alone, that drives the whistlers.

papers.title: Making Reconnection Cooler: A relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics model for radiative collisionless reconnection
papers.abstract: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely site for particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has substantially modelled such collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force countering the acceleration of the particles. Here, we systematically derive an energy-momentum sink term in relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription which reproduces the fast reconnection rate seen in kinetic calculations, to model radiative losses. We show that our radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties -- including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the out-flowing plasma -- for inverse Compton cooling applied to two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmarked to kinetic simulations. Our results hold in various cooling regimes with a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory. Our radiative model lays a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, such as in reconnection sites in a local turbulent flow or globally in the magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.

papers.title: Winding-Pack Quench Simulation of Stellarator Coils: Hydraulic Field-Network Coupling and Transverse Heat Conduction in OPENSC$^2$
papers.abstract: Quench propagation in cable-in-conduit conductors is thermo-hydraulically driven, yet a standalone 1D model treats a conductor as one straight adiabatic cable with prescribed pressure and mass-flow boundaries, so secondary quenches and flow redistribution between windings cannot be resolved without coupling to further, so far proprietary, codes. We extend the open-source code OPENSC$^2$ with transverse heat conduction between turns, a 3D field resolving the current-sharing temperature, induced losses, and a lumped hydraulic network coupled to the conductors by a mass-flow formulation. Compared to the 2006 W7-X coil tests, it predicts the quench site and cuts the outlet-temperature overestimation from 55 K to 25 K. The identified mechanisms indicate that the position of the helium inlets and outlets relative to the field, the hydraulic interconnection of the windings, the turn insulation and the current dump should be considered together in the quench design of future stellarator coils.

papers.title: 2D Magnetic Reconnection and Plasmoid Evolution in Partially Ionized Plasmas
papers.abstract: Magnetic reconnection in partially ionized plasmas is an important channel for energy release. While the plasmoid instability is well characterized in 2D fully ionized plasmas, its behavior in the presence of neutral-dominated plasma remains poorly understood in the nonlinear, high-Lundquist-number ($S = 10^5$) regime. We present high-resolution ($16384 \times 4096$ cells) isothermal two-dimensional two-fluid (ion $+$ neutral) simulations of Harris-sheet reconnection without ionization or recombination, comparing fully ionized and partially ionized (ionization fraction $\xi = 10^{-1}$ and $10^{-2}$) regimes. Ambipolar drift promotes early current-sheet thinning, while ion-neutral decoupling modifies the subsequent plasmoid evolution. During the simulated interval, the $\xi=10^{-2}$ run remains fragmented into a chain of small plasmoids, whereas the fully ionized run develops a macroscopic ``monster'' plasmoid. Below the neutral-ion decoupling scale $\ell_{\rm dec}$, ions concentrate into the plasmoids, reaching peak overdensities $\rho_i/\rho_{i,0} \approx 10$ ($\xi = 10^{-1}$) and $3-5\times10^{3}$ ($\xi = 10^{-2}$), while the neutrals remain comparatively smooth. This local pile-up raises the ionization fraction and recouples the two fluids within the plasmoids. Measured from the out-of-plane electric field at the reconnection sites, the reconnection rate in the $\xi = 10^{-2}$ case achieves $R_{\rm rec}\approx0.01$, whereas the $\xi = 10^{-1}$ case rises to a rate $\approx0.02$ and further to $0.035$ when apparent coalescence occurs. In the $\xi = 10^{-2}$ case, the ambipolar drift drives a rapid ion inflow $\sim0.5\,v_{A,0}$ into the layer at the same reconnection sites, far above the neutral inflow velocity $\sim0.1\,v_{A,0}$. Here, $v_{A,0}$ is the upstream total Alfv\'en speed.
